output.summary: The yield drop is real: customer PPM rose and CMM gauge R&R and the inspection program were stable. Three changes overlap in time. These are Corvane bar with rising hardness spread, a spindle service skipped since May with runout out of limit on L3-02 and L3-05, and the 12-hour shifts. The new-operator cohort is ruled out, because yield fell before they ran alone and their reject rate matches the experienced operators'. Fatigue is unproven, since scrap-tag times show when the tag was written, not when the part was cut. Steel and spindle cannot be separated yet. The best next step is to service the spindles in two staggered groups, run Tamsworth trial lots, and pull the Line 6 CMM data. Do not revert shifts as the root cause, cut inspection, or punish operators.
